title: Transit feasibility study and Broken Front Path heritage designation
subtitle: Surplus land sales, 2026 tax rates, park agreements, business park demolition contract and fee changes also approved.
overview: Council received the final Transit Feasibility Study, which recommends a phased transit system linking Fergus and Elora, with regional connections to Guelph, delivered through a shared service with Wellington County. Receiving the report commits the Township to nothing yet. Council discussed fares, free-ride options, funding sources and the county partnership.

Council also confirmed its intention to designate two properties on Broken Front Path in Elora as having cultural heritage value, and passed the designation by-law. It declared various Township parcels surplus and authorized the CAO to sign sale agreements, with proceeds meant for housing initiatives and part of the Operations Centre. It also set the 2026 tax rates and amended the Fees and Charges By-law.

Other approvals included a use of grounds agreement for the Kitchen in the Park Project in Bissell Park, a concession lease at Highland Park, and a demolition contract at the Centre Wellington Business Park. A public meeting was held on a zoning amendment at 7010 Third Line, and no members of the public spoke. Nothing was reported from the closed session.

decisions.detail: Council received the final study for information, which recommends phased transit service, a shared delivery model with Wellington County and a five-year implementation plan {{vote:m5}}.

decisions.item: Heritage designation, Broken Front Path, Elora
decisions.detail: Council confirmed its intention to designate 27 and 32 Broken Front Path Pvt. as properties of cultural heritage value and gave three readings to the designation by-law {{vote:m7}}.
Council declared various Township parcels surplus and delegated authority to the CAO to sign purchase and sale agreements {{vote:m12}}.
Council adopted the by-law setting the Township's 2026 tax rates {{vote:m13}}.
Council awarded Request for Quotation #30-26 to Bellamy Contracting Services Ltd. at $67,640.00, excluding contingency and HST, and revised the project funding {{vote:m11}}.

decisions.item: Kitchen in the Park use of grounds agreement
decisions.detail: Council authorized a Use of Grounds Agreement for a designated area of Bissell Park and delegated future extensions to the Managing Director of Community Services {{vote:m8}}.
Council authorized a lease agreement to operate the Highland Park concession booth in Fergus {{vote:m9}}.
Council passed amendments to the 2026 Fees and Charges By-law as outlined in report FIN2026-07 {{vote:m14}}.

debate: On transit, councillors asked about fares. One asked why there was no teen or student fare, and another wanted a free service like the current shuttle. The consultant said a small fare brings revenue that can pay for expanded service, and that free periods such as weekends or peak tourism season are an option.

Councillors asked about the county relationship, ownership of vehicles and external funding. The consultant said county staff had been involved throughout, and that provincial gas tax funding becomes available once service moves past a pilot. The consultant also said vehicle ownership could be shared or contracted, and that green vehicles could come later.

On the Broken Front Path designation, staff said they had received no information disputing the heritage value and no structural assessment. They noted the owner's legal counsel had objected and that a related demolition permit decision is in litigation. One councillor said they would vote against, doubting that forcing an objecting owner to act as steward was a good use of resources. Others said they favoured continuing the process begun in January.

On surplus property, one councillor noted that council had discussed a preference for medical use at the 205 Queen Street East building. The councillor also noted that the publicly owned riverfront piece would not be sold.

On the Kitchen in the Park agreement, one councillor asked whether a 60-day notice period was standard and suggested a safety barrier at Bissell Park. Staff said the notice term came from legal counsel and that the barrier idea would be reviewed.
